paragraphs.title: Punishment of the Forces of Evil

easy.explanation: The verse says the Lord will punish Leviathan and slay the dragon.
easy.q: Whom will the Lord punish in that day?

answers: His sore, great, and strong sword
easy.explanation: The verse describes the Lord’s sword as sore, great, and strong.
easy.q: What will the Lord use to punish Leviathan?

easy.explanation: The verse calls it the dragon that is in the sea.

answers: A piercing serpent and a crooked serpent
A small serpent and a great serpent
A desert serpent and a mountain serpent
medium.explanation: Leviathan is called the piercing serpent and the crooked serpent.
medium.q: How are the two forms of Leviathan described?

answers: The great power of the Lord’s judgment
That the event is an ordinary human battle
medium.explanation: The three strong descriptions emphasize the power of the judgment.
medium.q: What does the description of the Lord’s sword emphasize?
What does “crooked” mean in the phrase “that crooked serpent”?

answers: Punishment followed by a return to Jerusalem
Punishment with a sword followed by the slaying of the sea dragon
challenge.explanation: The Lord punishes Leviathan with a sword and slays the dragon in the sea.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of the Lord’s actions in the verse?

answers: Both are presented as threatening powers associated with the sea
Both are plants in a vineyard
challenge.explanation: Both are presented as dangerous supernatural powers, and the dragon is explicitly in the sea.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by Leviathan and the dragon?

answers: A change between two places in the land
Two descriptions of the same threatening power
challenge.explanation: The repeated name introduces the piercing and crooked descriptions of Leviathan.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by naming Leviathan twice?

easy.explanation: The passage begins with a song about a vineyard.
easy.q: What is Israel compared to in these verses?

answers: He leads it into the wilderness
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I do keep it” and “I will water it.”
easy.q: What does the Lord do for the vineyard?

answers: It will disappear from the earth
It will blossom and fill the world with fruit
easy.explanation: Jacob will take root, Israel will blossom, and the world will be filled with fruit.
easy.q: What will eventually happen to Israel according to the vineyard image?

answers: To turn it into a city
medium.explanation: The Lord keeps it continually so that nothing will hurt it.
medium.q: Why does the Lord keep the vineyard night and day?

medium.explanation: He says He would go through them and burn them together.
medium.q: What does the Lord say He will do with the briers and thorns?

medium.explanation: In this context, “keep” means to guard and protect.
medium.q: What does “keep” mean in “I the Lord do keep it”?

answers: Removing the thorns allows the vineyard to flourish and bear fruit
The thorns provide the vineyard’s fruit
The fruit causes the thorns to return
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the destruction of the thorns with the vineyard’s future fruitfulness.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between removing the thorns and the vineyard’s fruitfulness?

answers: A willingness to confront and destroy the thorns
A desire to plant thorns in the vineyard
challenge.explanation: The Lord challenges the thorns and declares that He would burn them.
challenge.q: What does the question “Who would set the briers and thorns against me in battle?” express?

answers: The one who takes hold of the Lord’s strength must make peace with Him
The vineyard must become a wilderness
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me.”
challenge.q: What condition for peace is stated in the passage?

answers: It is not the same as their punishment
easy.explanation: The verse asks whether the Lord has smitten Israel as He smote those who smote him.
easy.q: How is Israel’s punishment compared with the punishment of the enemies?

easy.explanation: The passage presents the punishment as measured and corrective.
easy.q: What is the purpose of the punishment described in these verses?

answers: They become chalkstones beaten in pieces
easy.explanation: The verse says the altar stones are made like chalkstones beaten in sunder.
easy.q: What happens to the stones of the foreign altar?

answers: It has no connection with correction
medium.explanation: “In measure” indicates that the punishment is limited and carefully administered.
medium.q: What does “In measure” teach about the Lord’s punishment?

answers: Purging includes removing the sinful practices
Purging removes the need for any change
medium.explanation: The verse connects Jacob’s cleansing with taking away his sin and destroying idolatrous objects.
medium.q: How is purging connected with the removal of sin?
What does “iniquity” mean in this passage?

answers: Israel receives measured correction, while the enemies are described as receiving harsher destruction
The enemies receive protection while Israel is abandoned
challenge.explanation: The comparison presents Israel’s punishment as measured and intended to correct.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the Lord’s treatment of Israel and His treatment of the enemies?

answers: Turning from idolatry and removing sin
Turning the altar into a vineyard
challenge.explanation: The destruction of these objects represents the removal of foreign worship.
challenge.q: What spiritual change is symbolized by destroying the altar stones, groves, and images?

answers: The removal of sin includes destroying the objects of false worship
Both statements concern gathering the exiles
The second statement cancels the first
challenge.explanation: The verse explains that purging sin involves removing the groves and images.
challenge.q: How are the two statements about purging iniquity and removing images related?

paragraphs.title: The Desolate City and Lack of Understanding

answers: It becomes desolate like a wilderness
easy.explanation: The city is described as desolate, forsaken, and like a wilderness.
easy.q: What happens to the defenced city?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the calf shall feed and lie down there.
easy.q: What animal feeds among the ruins?

answers: They are a people of no understanding
They build altars to the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says they receive no mercy because they are a people of no understanding.
easy.q: Why will the people not receive mercy?

medium.explanation: The drying and burning of the branches portrays desolation and destruction.
medium.q: What do the withered and burned branches represent in the passage?

answers: The abandoned city becomes a place where an animal can feed and lie down
The calf builds the city walls
medium.explanation: Because the city is forsaken, the calf grazes and rests among its remains.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the city’s abandonment and the calf’s presence?
What does “understanding” mean in “a people of no understanding”?

answers: People who do not understand and return to God do not receive mercy
Lack of understanding causes the vineyard to flourish
Mercy is given especially to those without understanding
challenge.explanation: The verse links the people’s lack of understanding with the Lord’s refusal to show mercy.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between lack of understanding and the absence of mercy?

answers: The vineyard is guarded and fruitful, while the city is forsaken and desolate
The city flourishes while the vineyard burns
challenge.explanation: The vineyard receives protection, but the city becomes a wilderness.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the vineyard in the earlier verses and the city here?

answers: That it is abandoned and left empty
challenge.q: What does the word “forsaken” emphasize about the habitation?

paragraphs.title: The Gathering of Israel and Return to Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The verse says they shall be gathered “one by one.”
easy.q: How will the children of Israel be gathered?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the great trumpet shall be blown.
easy.q: What will be blown to gather the scattered people?

easy.explanation: They will worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where will the gathered people worship the Lord?

answers: From the channel of the river to the stream of Egypt
From Jerusalem to the holy mount only
From the sea to the vineyard
medium.explanation: The verse gives the boundaries as the channel of the river and the stream of Egypt.
medium.q: From what region will the Lord gather the children of Israel?

answers: Those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt
medium.explanation: The trumpet gathers the scattered people in Assyria and Egypt.
medium.q: Who will come when the great trumpet is blown?

answers: People driven away or scattered from their home
People who remained in the city
People who work in the vineyard
medium.explanation: The outcasts are those who have been driven away or dispersed.
medium.q: What does “outcasts” mean in this passage?

answers: First a gathering from the region, then the trumpet call and worship in Jerusalem
First the city’s destruction, then the planting of the vineyard
First Leviathan’s punishment, then the burning of the thorns
challenge.explanation: The first verse describes gathering, and the next describes the trumpet, return, and worship.
challenge.q: What sequence is presented in the final two verses?

answers: The spiritual destination of the return
challenge.explanation: The gathering ends with the people returning to worship the Lord in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What does worshiping on the holy mount at Jerusalem emphasize?

answers: A personal and complete gathering of the Israelites
That only a few people will be gathered
That the people will be scattered again
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the careful gathering of each person.
challenge.q: What does “one by one” emphasize about the gathering?
